title: Planck's law against Rayleigh–Jeans
caption: Plotted against x = hf/k_BT, the classical Rayleigh–Jeans energy density grows as x² without limit (the ultraviolet catastrophe) while Planck's law, x³/(eˣ − 1), follows it at low x, peaks near x = 2.82 and is cut off exponentially. At x = 5 the ratio is 5/(e⁵ − 1) = 0.034 (Planck 0.85, Rayleigh–Jeans 25, off the top of the graph).
alt: Graph of energy density against hf over kT from 0 to 6: the Rayleigh–Jeans parabola rises off the top of the graph, while Planck's curve matches it at small x, peaks at about 1.4 near x = 2.8 and falls away.
description: The horizontal axis is x = hf/k_BT; the vertical axis is the energy density per unit frequency in units of 8π(k_BT)³/(hc)³.
The Rayleigh–Jeans curve is x²: it matches Planck's law only at small x, then climbs without bound.
Planck's curve x³/(eˣ − 1) rises, peaks at x = 2.82 (height 1.42) and then falls exponentially because quanta hf ≫ k_BT are rarely excited.
At x = 5: Planck = 0.85, Rayleigh–Jeans = 25, a ratio of 0.034.
